candidate.title: CirSeq
candidate.scope: The CirSeq RNA-virus circular sequencing row in the assigned Illumina schematic: genomic RNA fragment circularization, random-primed rolling-circle reverse transcription, repeat sequence comparison and error-corrected consensus. The whole-genome RNA icon supplies biological context; the linear-to-circular substrate is a genomic RNA fragment, as resolved by the primary papers. The library-to-sequence interface compressed into the drawing is kept broad. Neighboring TCR-LA-MC PCR and TIVA rows are separate catalogue entries, not alternatives to CirSeq. Circular sequencing and circular resequencing are names used for this RNA workflow by the two inspected primary papers. DNA Cir-seq and Droplet-CirSeq are outside this declared schematic scope.

states.label: Linear genomic RNA fragments from whole-genome RNA
features: Biological target: sequence variants in an RNA-virus population; the left icon is labeled Whole-genome RNA and carries an AA(A)n annotation.

The unlabeled purple linear substrate is interpreted as fragmented genomic RNA, not an intact genome that must fit into one sequencing read. Fragment preparation is input history, not a separately drawn transformation.
For the paper-supported implementation, fragment length permits about three template copies per sequencing read. The schematic does not label substrate end chemistry.

AA(A)n marks a poly(A)-tailed starting-RNA icon. The cited poliovirus implementation used poly(A)-selected RNA; the depicted copying step uses random primers. The icon does not establish a poly(A) requirement for every CirSeq implementation.

operations.label: Circularize RNA with kinase and RNA ligase 1
operations.description: Convert the linear genomic RNA fragment substrate into the closed circular RNA template. The primary protocol resolves the kinase role as 5′ phosphorylation before end joining; the fragment preparation preceding this input is not expanded into unshown execution steps.
operations.mechanism: Kinase-supported end preparation and RNA ligase 1-mediated RNA circularization; these are reagents acting on the RNA, not additional biological branches.
operations.information_effect: Preserve the sequence of one original RNA fragment in a reusable circular template, including any pre-existing variant.

operations.label: Random primers / Repeat 1, Repeat 2, Repeat 3
operations.description: Use random primers on the circular RNA template to initiate rolling-circle reverse transcription, creating a linear cDNA with multiple tandem copies of that same template. The circle in the product-side drawing is the copying template, not a second output library.
operations.mechanism: Repeated reverse transcription around a circular RNA template generates physically linked cDNA repeats. The orange short line is a primer reagent, not a sample branch.
operations.information_effect: Encode multiple observations of the same original RNA sequence on one DNA molecule. A template variant is copied into every repeat, whereas errors introduced while making individual copies can be discordant.

operations.information_effect: Convert physical within-molecule redundancy into aligned sequence data while retaining the association with one RNA template fragment.

operations.label: Corrected sequence
operations.description: Compare the aligned repeat bases and form a majority consensus. The shared magenta Mutation is retained; the dark discordant Error in one repeat is removed from the corrected sequence. This is computational sequence correction, not chemical repair of the RNA or DNA.
operations.mechanism: Majority logic consensus of the repeated observations.
operations.information_effect: Suppress discordant enzymatic/sequencing errors while retaining concordant template variants; the diagram illustrates error reduction, not guaranteed error-free or biologically exhaustive detection.
